title: Identifying Parts of a Noun Phrase

instruction.text: Select the noun in the noun phrase.

end.text: A noun is a person, place, or thing that is the subject of the noun phrase.

instruction.text: Select the adjective in the noun phrase.

end.text: An adjective is used to describe a noun.

instruction.text: Select the determiner in the noun phrase.

end.text: A determiner indicates what you are referring to in a noun phrase.

instruction.text: Select the noun in the noun phrase.

end.text: A noun is a person, place, or thing that is the subject of the noun phrase.

instruction.text: Select the two adjectives in the noun phrase.

end.text: An adjective is used to describe a noun.

instruction.text: Select the determiner in the noun phrase.

end.text: A determiner indicates what you are referring to in a noun phrase. You don’t always need a determiner.

atoms.b: A noun phrase is made up of a ((++noun verb)) and ((++one_or_more one three)) ((++adjectives verbs)). Often ((++determiners adverbs)) are used as well, to add more information.
If there is more than one adjective in a noun phrase, you have to add a ((++comma full-stop)) to separate them.
